title: Webhook operations console
summary: Receive, authenticate, deduplicate, inspect, replay, and diagnose external events through a usable operations interface.
outcome: An event-processing app with a durable inbox, explicit ordering assumptions, controlled replay, and evidence-based recovery.
prerequisites: Typed HTTP boundaries, transactions, worker lifecycle, and provider adapters. Use a local fake sender and generated payloads.
model: Endpoint: workspaceId, provider, secretVersion, enabled. EventReceipt: providerEventId, receivedAt, payloadVersion, digest.
ProcessingAttempt: eventId, generation, outcome, errorCategory, duration. Projection stores the domain state derived from accepted events.
ReplayRequest: scope, actor, reason, dryRun, generation. Redact or bound stored payloads according to the chosen retention policy.
boundaries: Raw request verification → decoded durable receipt → bounded worker → transactional domain projection. Replay uses the same handler with explicit generation and authorization.

milestones.title: Accept events into a durable inbox
milestones.brief: Receive a provider-shaped event, validate its envelope, persist it, and acknowledge only after the receipt is durable.
milestones.explanation: The acknowledgement tells a sender whether to retry. Returning success before durable receipt risks losing the event if the process crashes. Separate fast ingestion from potentially slow domain processing, bound body size, and keep the provider's event identity distinct from your internal receipt identity.
steps: Define the accepted envelope, size limit, provider event ID, response codes, and storage-failure behavior. Create valid and malformed fixtures.
Implement raw request limits, envelope decoding, and durable receipt insertion. Enqueue or discover pending receipts for later processing.
Fail persistence before commit, restart after commit, and submit a slow-to-process event. Verify response timing and stored state.

checks.label: Success acknowledgement follows durable receipt storage.
Malformed or oversized requests cannot enter the processing queue.
A restart discovers accepted but unprocessed events.

milestones.experiment: Commit the receipt, terminate the handler before its response, and resend the event. Explain why duplicate receipt handling is necessary even when ingestion succeeded.
milestones.review: Distinguish received from successfully applied. The operations interface should not label an accepted HTTP request as completed domain work.
milestones.stretch: Add backpressure that returns an appropriate retryable response when the durable queue cannot safely accept more work.

milestones.title: Verify signatures and rotate secrets
milestones.brief: Authenticate incoming callbacks using a provider's documented signing scheme, including key rotation and replay-window rules.
milestones.explanation: A signature usually covers exact bytes, so parsing and reserializing JSON before verification can change the signed material. Use the provider's specified algorithm, timestamp handling, and comparison method. Rotation requires an explicit overlap window, and test fixtures should use public teaching secrets rather than real credentials.
steps: Choose a documented provider-shaped signature contract and create fixtures for valid, tampered, expired, missing, and previous-key signatures.
Verify the raw body before trusting decoded fields. Supply current and allowed previous secrets through configuration without exposing them to the client.
Test rotation boundaries, malformed signature headers, clock skew policy, and a body whose whitespace changes after signing.

checks.label: Tampered or unauthenticated payloads never mutate domain state.
Old keys work only during the documented rotation overlap.
Verification matches exact signed bytes and the chosen replay policy.

milestones.experiment: Sign one JSON string, reformat its whitespace, and send the old signature. Verify the handler rejects it if the contract signs raw bytes.
milestones.review: Avoid inventing a generic signature scheme and calling it provider-compatible. Cite the specific provider contract used by your adapter.
milestones.stretch: Add a rotation rehearsal that measures rejection categories while keeping secret material out of diagnostic output.

milestones.title: Apply duplicate events once
milestones.brief: Process a repeated external event without applying its business effect more than once, including crashes at intermediate points.
milestones.explanation: A durable inbox prevents receipt loss but does not automatically prevent duplicate business writes. Protect processing receipt and mutation in a transaction or another explicitly justified protocol. Compare a repeated event's content digest so reuse of an event ID with different data does not silently masquerade as a harmless retry.
steps: Choose a simple projection, such as an external order state. Define duplicate identity and conflicting-payload handling.
Apply the event and mark its successful processing atomically. Keep failed attempts separate from a successful receipt.
Inject failures before mutation, after mutation but before commit, and after commit but before acknowledgement. Replay each fixture.

checks.label: Repeated identical events produce one committed business effect.
An event ID reused with different content is detected.
Intermediate failures leave the event safely retryable.

milestones.experiment: Crash after the projection update inside the transaction, then restart. Verify both the update and success receipt rolled back together.
milestones.review: Show the unique constraint and transaction scope. A query that checks for an event before an unconditional insert still leaves a concurrency window.
milestones.stretch: Run two workers on the same receipt and prove the projection remains correct.

milestones.title: Handle late and out-of-order events
milestones.brief: Apply events according to domain versions or transitions rather than assuming network arrival order represents business order.
milestones.explanation: An event received last may describe an older state. Choose an ordering strategy supported by the source: sequence numbers, resource versions, allowed transitions, or reconciliation against an authoritative read. Provider timestamps alone may not establish a total order. Preserve ignored or deferred events with a reason so operators can explain the result.
steps: Create sequences with duplicates, gaps, reversed delivery, and terminal states followed by older updates. Write the intended final projection for each.
Implement the chosen reducer policy and distinguish applied, ignored, deferred, and rejected outcomes.
Replay every ordering permutation that matters to the contract. Test missing predecessor recovery and bounded waiting for gaps.

checks.label: Equivalent supported event sequences produce the intended final state.
Older events cannot silently regress a newer authoritative version.
Deferred or ignored events retain a diagnosable reason.

milestones.experiment: Deliver completed before created for the same external resource. Verify the declared policy either reconstructs, defers, or reconciles safely.
milestones.review: Ask the agent to name the evidence supporting its ordering assumption. If the provider offers no reliable sequence, record that uncertainty in the design.
milestones.stretch: Add an authoritative reconciliation read and test how its result interacts with events arriving during the fetch.

milestones.title: Build a controlled replay interface
milestones.brief: Let an operator inspect failures and request a bounded replay with an explicit reason and a preview of intended effects.
milestones.explanation: Replay is a production mutation, not merely another read of stored JSON. Scope it by tenant, event set, handler version, and batch limit. Reuse the same validation and idempotency rules as normal processing. A dry run must avoid external writes; describe any effects it cannot predict rather than promising a perfect simulation.
steps: Design event search, attempt detail, and replay confirmation with actor, reason, range, and maximum count. Separate read-only operator and replay permissions.
Implement dry-run reduction against a disposable or isolated projection, then queue approved replay requests durably.
Test unauthorized replay, overlapping batches, a changed handler, and cancellation after some events have already committed.

checks.label: Only authorized operators can request mutations.
Dry runs perform no external writes and show bounded scope.
Replay uses normal correctness rules and records each outcome.

milestones.experiment: Start two overlapping replay requests for the same failed events. Verify processing identities or state guards prevent duplicate business effects.
milestones.review: Explain what cancellation can stop and which completed events remain committed. The interface should show partial progress honestly.
milestones.stretch: Add a downloadable replay report containing handler version, selected IDs, outcomes, and unresolved events.

milestones.title: Measure lag and recover from poison events
milestones.brief: Monitor queue age and failure categories, isolate repeatedly failing events, and rehearse recovery without blocking healthy work.
milestones.explanation: A queue can appear busy while one old event never progresses. Track age as well as size, separate retryable failures from permanent validation problems, and bound attempts. Quarantining a poison event should preserve evidence and a path to reviewed replay, while unrelated events continue processing according to their ordering dependencies.
steps: Define metrics for pending count, oldest age, throughput, attempts, and categorized failures. Set actionable thresholds for the sample workload.
Implement bounded retries and a quarantined state with redacted diagnostics. Keep per-resource ordering dependencies visible.
Inject one poison payload among healthy events, pause the provider, restart workers, and execute a written recovery procedure.

checks.label: Healthy independent events continue when one event repeatedly fails.
Metrics expose stalled age and categorized failure causes.
A recovery rehearsal accounts for every accepted receipt.

milestones.experiment: Create a payload that always fails after acquisition but before projection. Verify retries stop at the budget and operators can locate the exact receipt.
milestones.review: Record a timeline from alert to diagnosis to replay. Avoid logging complete sensitive payloads merely to make troubleshooting easier.
milestones.stretch: Deploy a handler fix with canary replay, compare projections, then expand the replay only after the observed result is correct.
